keys.description: The most CPU cores the VM can use
The most memory the VM can use, in MiB. Memory it isn't using goes back to your Mac
Create the fev Docker context and select it, so docker commands use Fevom
Include Fevom's data in Time Machine backups. It is one large disk image, which can make backups much larger
Let other devices on your network reach published ports. Ports published on 127.0.0.1 or ::1 stay on this Mac
Share your Mac's files with the VM, so containers can bind-mount Mac folders
Pause the VM while your Mac sleeps. Containers and machines carry on where they were when it wakes
Start Fevom in the background when you log in. The VM starts only when something needs it
Let containers reach servers on your Mac's localhost at host.docker.internal
Forward the ports machines listen on to localhost on your Mac
Let other devices on your network reach machines' ports that listen on all addresses (0.0.0.0 or ::)
The port of Fevom's SSH server, used by ssh fev
Let other devices on your network reach Fevom's SSH server. When off, only this Mac can connect
The IPv4 /16 Fevom takes its addresses from, chosen at the first start away from your Mac's networks. Changing it renumbers every container and machine
The IPv6 /48 (a unique local range) Fevom takes its addresses from, made at the first start
Reach containers and machines at their IP addresses from your Mac. Needs the admin helper (sudo fev setup --admin)
Serve fev.local names over HTTPS, with certificates from Fevom's own root certificate, which your Mac trusts after fev setup --https
The proxy for image pulls and for containers' and machines' connections: auto follows your Mac's settings, none uses no proxy, or enter a proxy URL
Hosts, domains and IP ranges (CIDR) reached without the proxy, in addition to your Mac's own exceptions
Send containers' and machines' TCP connections through the proxy, without proxy settings inside them
Use the admin helper for direct IP access, fev.local names on your Mac and ports below 1024. Install it with sudo fev setup --admin
Hide ~/Fevom from Finder's sidebar and the desktop. The folder stays at ~/Fevom
Run x86 Linux software (linux/amd64 images, amd64 machines and 32-bit programs) through translation in the VM

The x86-64 translator: auto uses Rosetta, and FEX for software known to fail under Rosetta; fex or rosetta forces one. 32-bit programs always use FEX. A machine's emulation setting or a container's dev.fevom.emulation label overrides it
Run the Docker engine. When off, docker commands are refused and Linux machines keep running
The Docker engine's host name, shown by docker info and to a swarm's nodes
The binary cache the Debug Shell's tools are downloaded from. A mirror must serve the cache's own signatures. Applies at the next download
Where the Debug Shell's command index is downloaded from. Empty uses the index that ships with Fevom. Applies at the next download
Run a single-node Kubernetes cluster beside Docker that can run your Docker images. The first start downloads about 250 MB. While on, it uses about a tenth of a CPU core and up to 2 GiB of memory
Let other devices on your network reach the cluster's NodePort services. When off, only this Mac can
Fields of the cluster's kubelet configuration (KubeletConfiguration) as a JSON object. Applying it restarts k3s; workloads keep running
Run metrics-server in the cluster, for kubectl top
Where the cluster's image archive is downloaded from at the first start. Empty uses k3s's release. Its SHA-256 is checked either way
Size in MiB of the window through which the VM reads large shared files from this Mac's memory; 0 turns it off
